items.title: 1.3 Uncertainty (ghair yaqeeni, pakka na hona) in measurement (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Kitab ke pages to aap bilkul theek gin sakte hain, magar kitab ki length napne ke liye koi napne wala instrument chahiye. Har instrument par sab se chhote division tak nishan lage hote hain (isay calibration kehte hain), aur yahi baat us ki accuracy (kitna sahi) ki limit tay karti hai. Kisi instrument se reading lein to us ki measurement ki limit us ke scale ka sab se chhota division hoti hai. Is liye har napi gayi quantity mein kuch na kuch uncertainty (pakka na hona) hoti hai. Measurement scale ke sab se qareebi nishan tak li jati hai. Zyada se zyada uncertainty ko instrument ke ek sab se chhote division ke barabar maana ja sakta hai; ise absolute uncertainty kehte hain. Millimetre wale metre rule par yeh ek millimetre hai. Example: agar kitab ka ek edge (kinara) 10.0 cm ke nishan par aur doosra 33.5 cm par ho, to length uncertainty ke saath yeh hai:

Iska matlab hai ke kitab ki asal (true) length 23.4 cm aur 23.6 cm ke darmiyan hai. Har end (sire) par uncertainty ±0.05 cm hai; dono milkar length mein 0.1 cm ki uncertainty banti hai, jo metre rule ke least count ke barabar hai. Uncertainty in tareeqon se likhi ja sakti hai:

blocks.text_alt: Fractional uncertainty = Absolute uncertainty / Measured value
ya Percentage uncertainty = (Absolute uncertainty / Measured value) × 100

blocks.text: Kitab pehle kehti hai ke zyada se zyada uncertainty ek poora chhota division (1 mm) hai, phir misal mein har reading par aadha division (±0.05 cm) leti hai. Dono readings ki ±0.05 cm add ho kar ±0.1 cm, yani ek poora least count, ban jati hai. Exam mein aam taur par ek reading ki absolute uncertainty = least count li jati hai.
blocks.title: Easy words mein

blocks.text: Uncertainty in Digital Instruments (digital instruments mein uncertainty)

Kuch modern (naye) instruments ka scale digital hota hai. Hum aam taur par pakke (certain) digits se ek digit aage tak estimate (andaza) lagate hain; digital scale par yeh aakhri digit ke upar neeche hone (fluctuation) ki shakal mein nazar aata hai. Agar aakhri digit 1 ya 2 tak badalta rahe to woh aakhri digit likh lein. Agar aakhri digit 2 se zyada badle to shayad reading par hawa ke jhonkon (air currents) jaisi kisi cheez ka asar hai. Wajah kuch bhi ho, zyada fluctuation ka matlab hai ke dikhaya gaya aakhri digit asal mein significant nahi.

Significant figures ki madad se reading ki uncertainty batana aasan ho gaya hai. Agar reading significant figures ke rule se likhi jaye to us ka aakhri digit, jo estimate (andaza) hai, batata hai ke reading kitni accurate (sahi) hai.

blocks.prompt: Ek digital balance lagatar 24.36 g, 24.37 g, 24.36 g dikhata hai, aur doosra 24.3 g, 24.9 g, 24.1 g. Har soorat mein kya record karna chahiye?
blocks.explanation: Pehla display aakhri digit mein sirf 1 badalta hai, to aakhri digit rakha jata hai: 24.36 g (taqreeban ±0.01 g). Doosra aakhri digit mein 2 se kahin zyada badalta hai, to hawa ke jhonke jaisi koi cheez reading hila rahi hai aur aakhri digit significant nahi; reading 24 g likhi jaye, ya pehle wajah door ki jaye.

items: Har instrument apne sab se chhote division tak hi parhta hai; is liye har measurement mein uncertainty hoti hai. Absolute uncertainty ≈ ek least count (metre rule par 1 mm).
Fractional uncertainty = absolute / measured value (napi gayi value); percentage uncertainty = fractional × 100.
Digital scale: 1 ya 2 tak badalne wala aakhri digit likhein; zyada fluctuation ho to woh digit significant nahi.
